CveFindings.Name: Apache Log4net: Silent log event loss in XmlLayout and XmlLayoutSchemaLog4J due to unescaped XML 1.0 forbidden characters
CveFindings.Description: [CVE-2026-40021](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w). Severity: MEDIUM. Both projects declare log4net 2.0.10, matching affected range <3.3.0. Attacker-influenced forbidden XML characters can suppress log events when affected XML layouts are used. The checked-in legacy configuration uses PatternLayout, not an affected XML layout; application exploitability is not established. Upgrade to 3.3.0 or later. This is a dependency-version exposure, not a confirmed application vulnerability.

CveFindings.Description: [CVE-2025-55315](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5rrx-jjjq-q2r5). Severity: CRITICAL. Existing eShopPorted assets resolve Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core 2.2.0 through Microsoft.AspNetCore 2.2.0 -> Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel -> Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. GitHub lists <=2.3.0 as affected by HTTP request smuggling/security-feature bypass and 2.3.6 as patched. Deployment and request-processing prerequisites were not verified. Upgrade to a supported patched framework dependency set; compatibility of an isolated transitive override is unverified. Fresh dependency resolution failed because Microsoft.WebApplication.targets was unavailable; existing assets are not proof of deployed versions.

Existing eShopPorted assets resolve System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.5.0 through Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticFiles 2.2.0 -> Microsoft.Extensions.WebEncoders -> System.Text.Encodings.Web, matching affected range >=4.0.0,<4.5.1. CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit bind attacker-supplied PictureFileName and persist it without confinement validation. PicController.Index combines the stored name with ~/Pics at lines 38-39, reads all bytes at line 44, and returns them at line 46. A client can submit a valid catalog entry with ../Web.config, then request its picture to retrieve application configuration readable by the worker identity. CatalogServiceMock likewise stores submitted objects. No application authorization filter protects catalog actions; antiforgery does not restrict a direct client with its own token. No extension allowlist guards the read; unknown extensions are returned as application/octet-stream. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH arbitrary file disclosure.

CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: Same arbitrary-file-read issue as CWE-22: PictureFileName is writable through catalog Create/Edit, and PicController.Index passes a relative traversal such as ../Web.config through Path.Combine directly into File.ReadAllBytes at line 44. There is no canonical-path containment check or filename restriction. Access is limited only by the application process file permissions. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH.

CweFindings.Name: Absolute Path Traversal
CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Explanation: Same arbitrary-file-read issue as CWE-22: catalog Create/Edit accept absolute PictureFileName values, including Windows drive-rooted paths. Path.Combine(webRoot, item.PictureFileName) discards webRoot when its second argument is rooted; File.ReadAllBytes and File return the targeted file. No rooted-path rejection or containment check exists. An attacker can retrieve any known file readable by the worker identity. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Explanation: CatalogController.Create/Edit accept and persist client-controlled PictureFileName. PicController.Index uses it as a filesystem resource identifier without confinement checks, reads the selected file at line 44, and returns it at line 46. A submitted value such as ../Web.config selects a resource outside Pics. Model validation does not restrict filenames, and client-side readonly UI is not a server-side guard. This is the same arbitrary-file-read issue as CWE-22/23/36, not an additional independent vulnerability. Confidence 9/10; impact HIGH.
